article.name: autoharness
article.summary: autoharness is a Claude Code plugin that learns and maintains native skill folders from work in a session. It captures bounded, redacted session evidence, asks a reflector to propose changes, and uses a deterministic promoter to validate and write them. The project records use-related signals for recall and lifecycle management; this is a pinned source review, not a runtime or benchmark evaluation.

who_what.text: The project README says it is built by Tigerless Labs and describes autoharness as a Claude Code plugin and self-learning skill layer, rather than a hosted memory service. Its outputs are native skill folders usable through the host's skill mechanism.

architecture.text: The durable memory unit is a directory containing a native SKILL.md and optional scripts, templates, assets, or references. A .sidecar.json stores operational ownership and counters; an append-only .ledger.jsonl stores change reasons and evidence references. The promoter materializes redacted session evidence as content-addressed Markdown under references/.

Global and project skill libraries are separate filesystem layers. A layer can be redirected through configuration; each skill has no embedded tenant or principal key. The sidecar marker created_by: agent identifies the managed pool so user-authored and installed skills are excluded from managed updates and lifecycle actions.

The hook pipeline captures session transcript bytes, then a reflector compares the episode with existing skills and submits a structured stage_skill intent. The deterministic promoter performs content and safety validation and is the only component that writes the managed skill tree.

behavior.text: The default reflection cadence is 50 tool calls, configurable; Stop checks the accumulated call counter and uses a child-session guard to prevent recursive reflection. SessionEnd can flush a positive tail. A manual /learn entry point uses the same proposal and validation route.

Capture reads from a byte watermark, bounds individual records and the total window, redacts before handoff, and never writes to the host transcript. A digest may summarize earlier exchanges. The reflector's tool records proposed create, update, patch, remove_file, delete, or suggestion operations with a reason and evidence; it does not receive a generic file-writing path for the managed tree.

The promoter validates the shaped result before writing. It places referenced subfiles and redacted evidence first, writes SKILL.md last as the visible commit point, stamps new skills as agent-created, and appends an action/reason/evidence entry. Rejected intents do not land; queued intents are drained and cleared after promotion.

Update replaces the full SKILL.md body; patch applies an old-string/new-string delta only when the old text matches exactly once. Subfiles can be added or removed through guarded paths. A whole-skill delete is archived out of recall, with its ledger and evidence carried along; the skill store provides restore, so archive is reversible rather than secure erasure.

At session start, the plugin lists its managed skills grouped by category and layer, within a byte cap; the host already supplies full skill descriptions. The host's native recall remains in place. A maintenance pass reviews the use rate after probation and archives unused skills or the lowest-rate mature skills when a layer exceeds capacity.

metrics.evidence: The plugin adds an index of managed skills to the host's native recall surface and tracks later use, but this source review ran no answer-quality, recall, or abstention probes.

A reflector can patch or replace a skill and records the change reason and evidence; the inspected representation does not define fact-level temporal validity or a stale-value scoring rule. No correction probes were run.
Whole-skill retirement moves a directory to an archive outside recall and preserves its evidence and ledger; restoration is supported. No post-delete probes or residual-copy audit were performed.

Project and global directories separate storage layers, and managed writes require the ownership marker. No principal authorization predicate is encoded in skill records, and no cross-layer isolation probes were run.

Each accepted create/update has a reason and redacted session slice linked in a per-skill ledger. That provides change provenance, not claim-level citations for answers; no evidence adjudication was run.

Capture uses a byte offset and bounded reads; counters are disk-backed constant-size read-modify-write operations, and the recall index is byte-capped. No timings or write-to-recall probes were collected.

The README describes zero third-party Python dependencies and configurable child reflector/curator models. The design stores plain skill and evidence files plus sidecars, ledgers, queues, counters, and run records; no token, charge, or corpus-attributed storage measurements were collected.

limits.text: This review is limited to selected documentation and source at the verified main head. It does not establish learning quality, whether a skill will be recalled when useful, correctness of edits, safety under adversarial session content, or reliability under concurrent host activity.

Storage layers are filesystem directories rather than an authorization system. Scope behavior therefore depends on host and filesystem access, and archived skills remain on disk; secure deletion and cross-user isolation are not established by this review.

Lifecycle usage rate is a proxy based on host-observed skill loads and reads. It is not a direct correctness or usefulness score; the source distinguishes use and view counters, but reads can include browsing/curation.
The project documents Claude Code as the current host. Behavior on other runtimes, including whether their hooks and native skill discovery provide the same recall path, was not established.

benchmark.text: Benchmark not run. No autoharness runtime, benchmark workload, tests, or builds were run for this review.
Project metric definitions and fixture describe portable proposed probes. Their case counts and protocol are not results for autoharness.
